doc.title: Donn Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 6, 2009

title: Competition for band spots and Colgate players
summary: Band personnel changes, Colgate piano and trumpet players, Derry Hall, and student attitudes.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: In the years you were here, obviously some members graduated and stuff. Was there competition to get into the Catatonic Five?

Yes there was. There were a horn player and a piano player, and they went off to form their own band, and then when we needed a piano player sometimes we used this one fellow. But the other guy on trumpet was not really tuned in that much. In fact, for a couple of years and when we went to Europe and when we went to Carnegie Hall, our piano player and trumpet player were from Colgate. And I don’t know how that happened. I mean we were desperate for a musician, a piano player and a trumpet player,

in September of whatever year it was that they joined the band. And I guess Emerson knew somebody at Colgate and said, “Gee do you know any guys that play,” and they said, “Yeah there’s these two guys. They’re both pretty good, the piano player is extraordinary, exceptional.” So he went to Europe with us but he couldn’t make the Carnegie Hall gig so we used another fellow who was part of the original Catatonic Five, Derry Hall, who was from Clinton. So I have to say that while a lot of the people here at Hamilton, the students, really liked the band — in fact we played for the college more than two or three occasions, big concerts, important concerts, jazz concert weekend for example — but the students were so busy with their studies. I mean even my roommate said, “How do you do this? How can you go to school, how can you pass this course if you’re out playing jazz all the time.” I mean they liked it and appreciated that somebody was doing it, but they weren’t interested in trying. They left their horns at home when they went to college.
